reading_plan: Using life cycle assessment to drive innovation for sustainable cool clouds (peer_reviewed_paper) is a Nature Analysis article. Its compact two-column prose alternates between explanatory passages, technical definitions, quantitative tables, figures and detailed Methods. I take short steps around changes in the comparison, dense model assumptions and visual evidence, and longer steps through the framing and recommendations. I follow the body in reading order, taking figures and tables with the passages that invoke them, then continue through Methods and the extended data in PDF order.

A physical core can independently perform processor functions and may correspond to more than one logical core; logical core count is physical cores times threads per core. Packing density concerns devices or circuits per chip area.

claims.text: The Methods use-phase equation multiplies IT capacity in MW by load factor, PUE and 8,760 hours per year to obtain annual electricity in MWh.

PUE is total facility energy divided by energy delivered to IT. Load factor is the share of IT capacity in use; a conservative utilization assumption is used in design capacity and equipment planning.

Restrooms, cafés and irrigation are excluded on the assumption that staffing and non-cooling water are similar across designs. Two locations with dry and humid climates illustrate how cooling water needs change when temperatures cross a threshold.

All three cooling families use evaporative AHUs for server rooms. Cold plate adds copper tubing and CDUs, while immersion uses fluid coolers that can run dry in most climates and turn to adiabatic operation when more capacity is required.
Adiabatic cooling uses more water but can be more efficient than dry operation, especially in warm dry climates.
